Later we bought cold drinks from a small shop near the gate. We met a man with a dog and said hello as we passed. On the way home the bus was full so we had to stand all the way back to town. We cleaned the rooms and washed the clothes and made cakes in the kitchen. My son drew a dog on paper and my girl sang songs she had learned at school. In the evening my brother came round with his wife and kids for tea. We talked about work and school and plans for the next week. They left late at night after the rain had stopped. On the third day the sun came back and we went out to the shops in town. We bought milk and eggs and bread and some meat for the week. Then we came home and put it all away. My wife called her mother on the phone and talked for a long time. I sat in the yard and read the news in the paper. The kids played ball with the dog next door. At night we all ate together and told stories about past trips and good times we had known.
